_comment: Single source of truth for documentation drift: which source areas, when changed, require which docs (and which screenshots) to be updated. Read by .claude/hooks/doc-drift.py (the Stop hook) and by the /doc-sync command (.claude/commands/doc-sync.md). Source globs use fnmatch semantics against repo-relative POSIX paths; note that '*' also matches '/'. A rule is 'satisfied' for a session when at least one of its 'docs' files is in the changed set. Screenshots are listed for regeneration guidance (via scripts/screenshots/capture.py --only <names>); they do not themselves satisfy a rule. The contract (docs/protocol.md + docs/fixtures/) is intentionally NOT covered here - it is guarded by /contract-check and CI.

rules.why: The single-page fleet console. Any visible change to tabs, widgets, KPI tiles, charts, action buttons, deep-link hashes, or themes drifts the widget-by-widget reference and its screenshots.
rules.adr: Pure UI-layout tweaks need no ADR - record them in the commit message (CLAUDE.md).

rules.why: The /api/* routes that feed the dashboard. A change to their response shape changes what the dashboard renders and what the reference describes.
rules.adr: Route-shape changes are usually implementation detail; add an ADR only if a boundary moves.

rules.why: Authoritative server-side health thresholds. The telemetry reference quotes exact thresholds and the Overview/Flagged/reliability views are driven by them.
rules.adr: New health model / status semantics may warrant an ADR; a threshold tweak does not.

rules.why: Fleet aggregation, trends, forecasts, AI recommendations, and change diffs shown on Overview and Agent detail.
rules.adr: Add an ADR only if the analytics model (not the numbers) changes.

rules.why: Web activity, the per-host web filter, and screen time.
rules.adr: A change to the filter's trust/precedence model is architectural (see ADR-0024); the list editor UI is not.

rules.why: Who may sign in to a PC: the account_* tools, the accounts panel, and the local_accounts/logon_failures sections behind them. Local and Microsoft accounts share one surface, so a change to what is possible for one changes the reference for both.
rules.adr: Changing what kenny may do to an account, or the privacy line around naming accounts, is architectural (see ADR-0042); a panel-layout tweak is not.

rules.why: Push alerts on health transitions, inventory-change notifications, disk/battery forecasts, and the weekly digest.
rules.adr: A change to the alert model (transitions/scopes) may warrant an ADR (see ADR-0027).

rules.why: The capability/orchestration tool catalog and the confirm-gate the tool reference documents.
rules.adr: Adding/renaming a tool is a CONTRACT change: change docs/protocol.md + docs/fixtures/ and run /contract-check first.

rules.why: The runtime settings catalog exposed by the dashboard settings editor (ADR-0032) and documented in setup.
rules.adr: A new settings surface may warrant an ADR; adding one knob does not.

adr_rule.why: A record number is an address a reader follows from a code comment, so the set has to stay internally consistent: gap-free 0001..N numbering, an index that matches the directory, and citations that resolve.
adr_rule.note: Checked by .claude/hooks/doc-drift.py whenever a session touches a record, the index, or a file citing one: the numbering must be a gap-free 0001..N, every record must have an index row pointing at its real filename (and vice versa), and every ADR-NNNN citation or adr/NNNN- link anywhere in the repo must resolve. Implementation rationale belongs in the code it explains, never in a second kind of document.
